comments.body:
I had a quick thought about this. Would it be of interest if I could write a small command that copies dir modtimes from one remote to another (for backends that support it)? It would be intended as more of a short-term stop-gap to tide us over while we wait hopefully for full dir metadata support, which would be a much more complicated project.

Many backends (including `local` and `drive`) already support listing directory modtime, like:

```
rclone lsf --dirs-only -R --format "pt" src_remote:path
```

So the command I'm imagining would do basically the equivalent of the above command, then loop through all the results and do something like  `err = dir.SetModTime(ctx, t)`  for each corresponding dir on the dest. (Probably with a `--modify-window` check first, and maybe also support for `--update`.)

An alternate approach might be to tack it on to the end of `copy`/`sync` as an optional extra step, very much like `--create-empty-src-dirs`.

My use case is that my Google Drive currently has all the correct modtimes of my folders, and when I use rclone to `sync` them to a new computer, I want to be able to follow that with a command to copy over all the folder modtimes from `drive` to `local`. Modtime is the main piece of dir metadata I care about (especially because of [macOS "packages"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Package_(macOS)) which are really dirs), so in my opinion, a command like this would deliver a lot of value for relatively little effort. 

Is this something you'd want?

I have made a first pass at making sync preserve the folder modtimes/metadata here:

[v1.66.0-beta.7695.b8c0d3318.fix-6685-dir-sync](https://<redacted-host>/branch/fix-6685-dir-sync/v1.66.0-beta.7695.b8c0d3318.fix-6685-dir-sync/) on branch [fix-6685-dir-sync](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/fix-6685-dir-sync)

This is an early beta for comments and testing. It is missing a lot of integration tests so may not work properly!

It has some of your commits in @participant4 - thank you! - I re-used them for setting directory modtimes. I renamed the method to `DirSetModTime` which is not as nice as `TouchDir` but is consistent with the other methods and doesn't imply directory creation. Note that it also updates some bisync golden tests in b8c0d3318e9a4137dc8991904dbc3b31ce2be56b in a very minor way.

Here are some notes on how it works and what needs to be done. It also describes how to update a backend to support Directory modtimes or to support Metadata on directories.

## Notes

A non metdata sync will sync directory modtimes. This is a change from
the existing code but I think it will be welcomed by users. The reads
directory ModTime and sets them using DirSetModTime if available (or Directory.SetModTime).

A `--metadata` sync will read directory metadata (including mod times)
using Metadata and set them with SetMetadata

Syncs with and without metadata may have an additional pass afterwards
to SetModTimes of directories if they change when files are added (the
`DirModTimeUpdatesOnWrite` feature flag).

FIXME directory wrapping these backends needs fixing to proxy to underlying Directory
- combine
- crypt
- union

They all just need to override the path in the Directory so maybe a generic class to do that is needed.

FIXME need to kill off NewDirCopy - in use by crypt and is wrong -
need to make Directory wrapper and proxy everything else to the
underlying Directory

## TODO

- sync: tests
- sync: paralellize setDelayedDirModTimes
- operations: tests
- don't set metadata if it is already set
- don't set modtime if it is already set
- fstests: tests for new features
- docs - should SetDirModTime/MkdirMetadata be in the overview?
- more backends
- make sure we wrap methods on fs.Directory (SetModTime, SetMetadata etc) in all the wrapping remotes
- can make rclone touch work on directories
- stats! for mkdir/update metadata changes that happens operations?

fstests
- DirSetModTime
- MkdirMetadata
- Directory.Metadata
- Directory.SetModTime
- Directory.SetMetadata
- make sure Directory does not type assert to fs.Object or fs.ObjectInfo
- check any backend with MkdirMetadata should support setDirModTime
- Check if a backend advertises `WriteDirModtime` then it must allow directories to be created with metadata (MkdirMetadata).
- Check if a backend advertises `WriteDirSetModTime` then it must allow directories to be created with modtime (MkdirMetadata).
- go test -v -run TestIntegration/FsCheckWrap should check Directories are wrapped properly

## To add directory metadata to a backend

Decide on feature flags

```
ReadDirMetadata:          true,
WriteDirMetadata:         true,
WriteDirSetModTime:       true,
UserDirMetadata:          true,
DirModTimeUpdatesOnWrite: true/false,
```

Make `List` and `ListR` return specialized directory objects satisfying these interfaces

```
fs.Directory
fs.SetModTimer
fs.SetMetadataer
```

Remember assertions.

Implement the optional method `MkdirMetadata`. This should create a
directory with the metadata given. At minimum the backend should
interpret the `mtime` metadata to set the modification time.

It can implement `DirSetModTime` too but (I think!) rclone will work without it.

### SetModTime only

If a backend can only set modtime on directories and doesn't have directory metadata

```
ReadDirMetadata:          false,
WriteDirMetadata:         false,
WriteDirSetModTime:       false,
UserDirMetadata:          false,
DirModTimeUpdatesOnWrite: true/false,
```

This does not need to make `List`/`ListR` return specialized directory
objects. Instead it should implement a `DirSetModTime` optional
method.

This is a much simpler integration.

comments.body:
I played around with this a bit today and I think it's super great! It works pretty much exactly like I hoped it would 😃 

A few minor thoughts for you to do with as you will:

- Looks like the root is ignored, even when it's a subpath of the remote root. For example:

```
rclone sync /downloads/FolderA /downloads/FolderB
```

`FolderB` does not end up with the modtime from `FolderA`, but `FolderB/sub1` does get the modtime of `FolderA/sub1`. I understand why this is, but I wonder if it will be surprising for new users. (Also on macOS, where we have "packages" that are directories displayed like files, I imagine some users may try `copyto` on a `file.logicx` package and wonder why their copied "file" has the wrong modtime.)

- It looks like `MkdirMetadata` is capable of making parents but not of setting metadata on the parents it makes. For example, if `/a` exists and you `MkdirMetadata` `/a/b/c`, `c` gets metadata but `b` does not. I think that makes sense -- can't imagine how it could work otherwise, as we don't have any info about `b`. And I suppose callers can make `b` first, if they want to. 
- I think it would be nice if the `SkipDestructive` messages could include the name of the dir, and ideally also the time it would be setting. Some of them do include the dir (`MkdirModTime`) but others (`SetDirModTime`, `CopyDirMetadata`) just include the Fs root.
- Would also be nice to get an `INFO` message saying what it updated during non-dry runs.
- `CopyDirMetadata` living in `operations` seems like a slight departure from the way object metadata works where the dest backend is usually in charge of calling `fs.GetMetadataOptions`, but I don't think that's a bad thing -- just noting the difference. 
- Now that dirs are more than just implied paths and have properties of their own, I wonder if it would be worth considering additional filtering options for them. For example, I'm thinking ahead to `bisync` which is going to want to update some dir modtimes in one direction and others in the opposite direction, like it can easily do for files with a `--files-from` filter. Currently this would be difficult for dirs, as they only get included when their contents are included, and probably whichever direction is synced first would control the outcome (regardless of whether a src dir modtime is newer/older than the dst). I think we should be able to get around this fairly easily by doing our own `MkdirMetadata` pass after the `sync` calls, but if there was (say) a `--dirs-from` filtering option, we could probably eliminate this extra step, which would be more efficient. Just a thought!
- Relatedly, I wonder if the `--files-only` and `--dirs-only` options from `lsjson` would be useful to have as filtering options globally.

Awesome work -- can't wait for this to be finished! 🥳

I chose that design to minimise the backend code to write, but you are right it is a departure.

> * Now that dirs are more than just implied paths and have properties of their own, I wonder if it would be worth considering additional filtering options for them.

Currently rclone's filtering system almost entirely ignores directories and just works on files. We have these flags which can filter metadata on files but they could/should work on directories too

      --metadata-exclude stringArray        Exclude metadatas matching pattern
      --metadata-exclude-from stringArray   Read metadata exclude patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)
      --metadata-filter stringArray         Add a metadata filtering rule
      --metadata-filter-from stringArray    Read metadata filtering patterns from a file (use - to read from stdin)
      --metadata-include stringArray        Include metadatas matching pattern
      --metadata-include-from stringArray   Read metadata include patterns from file (use - to read from stdin)

Just a thought!

You can effectively do `--dirs-from` using `--include /path/to/dir/**` repeated, but do you mean just include the directories, or include the contents too?

> * Relatedly, I wonder if the `--files-only` and `--dirs-only` options from `lsjson` would be useful to have as filtering options globally.

Hmm, possibly. So you are thinking `--dirs-only` would just sync the directories?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
> You can effectively do `--dirs-from` using `--include /path/to/dir/**` repeated

`--include` has no effect when combined with `--files-from`, so I'm not sure this would work for bisync's purposes (bisync uses `--files-from` to specify which specific files should be synced in each direction.)

An example: suppose you are bisyncing `Path1` and `Path2`. `Path1/FolderA` and `Path2/FolderA` both contain some changed files, but overall `Path1/FolderA` has the newer directory modtime. If bisync does the equivalent of `rclone sync Path2 Path1` followed by `rclone sync Path1 Path2`, there's currently no way to ensure that the `Path1/FolderA` modtime overwrites `Path2/FolderA` instead of the reverse. The `Path2` dir times would always win, because of the sync order.

To put that another way: it's not possible to avoid losing the `Path1/FolderA` dir modtime during the first sync, while still syncing files under `Path1/FolderA` such as `Path1/FolderA/file.txt`.

So what I'm imagining instead is something like:
```
rclone sync Path2 Path1 --files-from files2to1.txt --dirs-from dirs2to1.txt
rclone sync Path1 Path2 --files-from files1to2.txt --dirs-from dirs1to2.txt
```
where `dirs1to2.txt` would contain `/FolderA` but `dirs2to1.txt` would not (while `files2to1.txt` and `files1to2.txt` would both contain different files under `/FolderA`.)

Another scenario where this comes up is empty dirs. It's currently impossible to sync with both `--files-from` and `--create-empty-src-dirs`, as an empty dir will never be deemed "included" if `--files-from` is in use.

> So you are thinking `--dirs-only` would just sync the directories?

Yes.

comments.body:
Ah yes, this is why the Bisync testing suite is both my best friend and greatest enemy 😆 The upside is it's nearly impossible to break something without it being detected. The downside is it will also detect intentional changes and unimportant differences in log output. 

(As an aside, the argument could definitely be made that they are ["Change-Detector Tests"](https://<redacted-host>/2015/01/testing-on-toilet-change-detector-tests.html) and should eventually be rewritten as proper unit tests... although I also think it would be very hard to write unit tests that cover all important outcomes. Bisync is a lot more complicated than Sync.)

> I put the modtime in the log but I think I might have to remove that or the INFO logs as it makes the bisync tests unstable. What do you think?

Rather than remove a useful feature to satisfy the tests, I think it would be better to improve the tests to accommodate the new feature. Here's how I think that could be done:

1. "Goldenize" with the following command:

```
go test ./cmd/bisync -remote local -golden
```

Check the unstaged changes carefully to ensure they are all intentional, then stage them.

2. Run the tests again to see what it is still picking up. This will often be ["logHoppers"](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L97-L124) -- log lines which can appear in a nondeterministic order due to concurrency, but are ultimately unimportant to the outcome and should not be considered a failure. These can be whitelisted with regex [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L97-L124).

3. For lines like [this](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/actions/runs/8055791513/job/22003427649#step:12:3837) which have a printed timestamp which would change from test to test, they will either need to be ignored (can do that with regex [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L61-L89)) or made deterministic (probably better, but harder). This same problem came up with file modtimes and there is a section of code [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L314-L323) that deals with that and could probably be modified to include dirs (removing that `&& !info.IsDir()` would probably help!) But I think that would get us only part of the way there, as the messages would still differ on backends without dir modtime support (or even with a different `Precision()`). There is some existing code [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L1380-L1404) that deals with a similar problem, but only in the listing files (not logs). So, adding a new [`dropMe`](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L61-L89) might be the easiest way to go here.

An alternative option would be to make a new ["Replacer"](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go#L1424-L1469) for it, which instead of ignoring it, keeps it in the logs but normalizes it to a glob variable to be consistent across platforms.

It's a very clever system that Ivan came up with, but complicated 😅

Happy to take on some of this so you can keep focusing on the important stuff -- just let me know!

> Should I add a sigil to logger for metadata/modtime updates - would that help?

Ultimately that is what should happen, although I think it won't make a difference until [this](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/8f0e9f9f6bd78f6ac7488ac48bbe7e9a9ba418ab/cmd/bisync/deltas.go#L194-L195) is removed (dir modtimes are explicitly ignored, since it wasn't previously possible to change them.) There are a few things like that in bisync which will warrant revisiting in this new paradigm (the filtering conversation is another), but I think it's ok if that has to what til Phase 2 -- it need not delay the `v1.66` release.

@participant9 
> The Date Modified for the folders working for rmount+winfsp (Windows) on the S3 compatible object store layer work correctly in this new version?

If you add `directory_markers = true` to your config

      --s3-directory-markers   Upload an empty object with a trailing slash when a new directory is created

Then directories will have a persistent date - otherwise they don't actually exist.

I don't think syncing directory modification times or metadata will work with `directory_markers` yet though. If you'd like to see this please open a [new issue](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/new/choose) about it. If you are working on behalf of a company you might be interested in taking out a [support contract](https://rclone.com/support) and we could add that as part of it.
